verses.text: Now about spiritual gifts, family—I don’t want you left in the dark.
You remember how, before you believed, people kept leading you off toward speechless idols, however they wanted.
So know this: nobody speaking by God’s Spirit says, “Jesus is cursed.” And nobody can truly say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.
There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit gives them.
There are different ways to serve, but the same Lord.
There are different kinds of work, but the same God powers all of it in everyone.
The Spirit’s presence is shown through each person for the good of everybody.
One person gets a message of wisdom through the Spirit; another gets a message of knowledge through that same Spirit;
another receives faith from the same Spirit, and another gifts of healing from that same Spirit;
another works miracles, another speaks God’s message, another can discern spirits, another speaks different languages, and another interprets those languages.
The one and same Spirit makes all these things happen, handing out gifts to each person as he chooses.
Think of the body: it’s one body with many parts, and all those parts together make one body. Christ is like that.
By one Spirit, we were all baptized into one body—Jew or Greek, enslaved or free—and we all drank of one Spirit.
The body isn’t one part. It’s got many.
If the foot says, “I’m not a hand, so I don’t belong to the body,” that doesn’t make it any less part of the body.
If the ear says, “I’m not an eye, so I don’t belong to the body,” it still belongs.
If the whole body were an eye, how would it hear? If it were all hearing, how would it smell?
But God put every part exactly where he wanted it in the body.
If the body were only one part, where would the body be?
But there are many parts and one body.
The eye can’t tell the hand, “I don’t need you!” And the head can’t tell the feet, “I don’t need you!”
Actually, the body parts that seem weaker are the ones we really need.
We give extra honor to parts we think are less honorable, and cover up the parts we’d rather not show.
The parts we’re comfortable showing don’t need that extra cover. God put the body together and gave more honor to the part that had less,
so there wouldn’t be divisions in the body, but every part would care for the others equally.
When one part hurts, every part feels it. When one part gets honored, every part celebrates.
You are Christ’s body, each of you an individual part of it.
God placed different people in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracle workers, healers, helpers, leaders, and people who speak different languages.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Does everyone work miracles?
Does everybody have healing gifts? Does everyone speak in different languages? Does everyone interpret?
Keep pursuing the greater gifts. And now I’ll show you a way that’s better than anything else.
